stories.title: Burnham 'increasingly confident' PC Harper's killers will not be released early
stories.summary: PM Andy Burnham said he is increasingly confident he can adapt the early release scheme to exclude the killers of PC Andrew Harper, after intense public and political pressure forced a policy review.

stories.title: UK extreme heat prompts COBRA emergency meeting
stories.summary: Andy Burnham convened a COBRA meeting with ministers and emergency agencies as temperatures hit 33°C across the UK, with up to 38°C forecast for Thursday.

stories.title: Will Andy Burnham's 'everyday fixes' be enough to get the public on his side?
stories.summary: Analysis of Burnham's governing approach argues his popular small-scale fixes are welcome but voters are yet to be convinced he can handle the 'big things' — with the prisons crisis as an early stress test.

topics.name: Burnham Gov Intelligence
topics.description: Procurement, tech/AI, spending, vendor & priority signals

stories.title: Post Office reveals additional £14.4m deal for Horizon replacement system
stories.summary: The Post Office has disclosed an additional £14.4m contract for its Horizon replacement, noting there is 'no third-party way to customise' the solution — raising procurement lock-in concerns.

stories.title: G-Cloud 15 launched to expand SME opportunities in cloud procurement
stories.summary: The latest G-Cloud framework has been launched with a focus on opening up cloud procurement to small and medium-sized enterprises across government.

stories.title: DSIT watchdog head grills government over departmental shake-up
stories.summary: The head of the DSIT watchdog questioned ministers about the government's departmental restructuring, raising accountability concerns over tech and digital governance.

topics.name: Parliament
topics.description: House of Commons, Lords, PMQs, debates, legislation

stories.title: Parliament in summer recess — no sittings this week
stories.summary: The House of Commons did not sit on 11 August 2026 due to the summer recess. No PMQs or major legislative debates are scheduled.

stories.title: Probation officers vote for strike action over early release scheme
stories.summary: Probation officers voted overwhelmingly for industrial action, warning that the prisoner early release scheme will add unsustainable workloads to an already stretched service.

stories.title: Burnham denies plans to scrap stamp duty ahead of October budget
stories.summary: The PM denied plans to reduce or abolish stamp duty, amid media speculation about property tax reforms ahead of the 28 October budget.

stories.title: Households near new pylons to get £250 off annual energy bills
stories.summary: The government announced that households living near new power pylons will receive £250/year off their energy bills, as it pushes ahead with 40+ grid upgrade projects.

stories.title: Kemi Badenoch faces questions over former neo-Nazi advisory role
stories.summary: Reports emerged that Kemi Badenoch gave a former neo-Nazi an advisory role, prompting criticism and questions about Conservative Party vetting processes.

stories.title: Conservatives attack government over prisoner early release scheme
stories.summary: Kemi Badenoch and Conservative MPs have been vocal in attacking the Burnham government's prisoner early release policy, seeking to capitalise on public anger over the PC Andrew Harper case.

stories.title: Lib Dem MP questions 'pressure' from No. 10 on sacked Foreign Office chief
stories.summary: Liberal Democrat MP Edward Morello raised questions in an inquiry about whether the recently sacked Foreign Office official faced pressure from Downing Street, probing civil service independence.

topics.name: Reform UK
topics.description: Nigel Farage, party news and announcements

stories.title: Farage resigns as Clacton MP, triggering by-election
stories.summary: Nigel Farage has resigned as MP for Clacton, forcing a by-election in his own constituency — described as a 'high-risk gamble' as he will need to fight to reclaim his own seat.

stories.title: 'Posh George' Cottrell moves business into Reform UK HQ building
stories.summary: George Cottrell, the convicted fraudster who secretly bankrolled Farage, has moved his company's address to the same building as Reform UK's headquarters.

stories.title: Reform UK 'Patrons' Club' donor linked to BNP campaigning
stories.summary: A figure in Reform UK's major donor circle was previously involved in campaigning for the British National Party, fuelling scrutiny of the party's donor base.

stories.title: SNP demands Burnham honours Labour's £300 energy bill pledge
stories.summary: The SNP called on PM Burnham to deliver on Labour's pre-election promise to cut energy bills by £300, as Burnham embarks on a cost-of-living tour of the UK.

stories.title: Nicola Sturgeon publicly criticises SNP for lacking 'vision' on independence
stories.summary: Former First Minister Nicola Sturgeon has openly criticised the SNP for failing to sell the case for independence effectively, adding to the party's internal tensions.

stories.title: CalMac ferry fines hit £21.3m as island communities demand action
stories.summary: Island communities are demanding greater accountability after CalMac ferry operator fines reached £21.3m, with First Minister Swinney confirming a £10m resilience fund.

topics.name: Cabinet Office
topics.description: Government reshuffles, senior appointments, cross-department policy

stories.title: Government advertises senior Government Chief IT Operations Officer role
stories.summary: The Civil Service has advertised a senior Government Chief IT Operations Officer position (salary £86,000–£117,800), signalling continued investment in strengthening central government's technology leadership.

stories.title: Home Office overhauls pre-smartphone-era police disclosure rules
stories.summary: The Home Office announced reforms to police disclosure rules — written before smartphones existed — to be overhauled, freeing up officer time as part of the government's public safety reform agenda.

stories.title: Clacton by-election called after Farage resigns — Labour leads polls for first time since March
stories.summary: Nigel Farage's resignation has triggered the Clacton by-election. Politico reports Labour has topped its poll of polls ahead of Reform for the first time since March, suggesting the government's rehabilitation is reflected in voting intention.
